claim: The delay a type prints `FL Dly` against and the loop it prints `FL Fb` against are, in both types that print them inside a larger chain, the delay and the loop of the stereo flanger that stands alone. Read as a comb at two settings of the delay byte and on both signs of the loop, all four readings of each type return the single type's figures exactly: 0.618 ms at a delay byte of 6 and 1.318 ms at 13 with the loop in phase, 0.624 and 1.296 with it inverted. That holds where the chorus runs into the flanger and where it sits beside it, so neither arrangement carries a delay line of its own. The teeth are 22.58 dB deep at the shallowest against the 16.05 dB the deepest of these records asks of one, and each profile scores as a comb of that spacing by at least 1.55 times what the same profile scores read on the other sign -- which is the control a filter sitting somewhere cannot imitate, since a peak scores the same either way. The modulator behind that delay is the single type's too, on the type the chorus runs into it. Its rate byte returns a table over ten settings whose four published ones are the single flanger's to four figures -- 1.6499 against 1.65, 4.9994 against 4.9993, 6.1007 against 6.0974, 9.9991 against 9.9986 Hz -- and the settings between them fall on the same line. Its depth byte buys the single flanger's excursion at every setting either run reads, to within 1.71 per cent against the 0.42 per cent one setting taken twice repeats to. On the type the chorus sits beside, the modulator is not read here: the reading that returns a rate picks a period out of an autocorrelation, and on that type the frequency series of a partial stands taller at twice the rate than at it at most settings of the flanger's feedback byte and carries nothing at the rate at all at the centre of it, which is where every run that is not asking about the loop parks that byte.
adds: The single type's claim says the byte is a loop and says what it is around. It says that on one type. These two print the same pair of bytes at the same addresses over the same printed ranges, and nothing structural had been read on either of them -- the only claims naming them were the two that run across every type, about what a parameter powers up holding and about what happens to a byte its page prints no state for. What is added is that the stage a combination names after another type is that type's stage, read on the one quantity a delay line cannot fake: where its comb sits.
refutedBy: A comb in either combination that sits at a spacing the single type does not return, at either delay setting or on either sign of the loop. One reading off the single type's two figures by more than the width the fit reports would say the stage is named after something it is not.
whatItWouldChange: Rendering either type needs one delay line and one loop, with the milliseconds the single type's table gives, rather than a second table read off these types. Thirty of this unit's sixty-five types are combinations named after others, and this is the second stage to be asked whether the name reaches the block -- after an equaliser section, and with the same answer.

values: What else the run had written when it took these readings. A type with more than one modulator returns whichever dominates, so a reading taken with the other stage turned down and one taken with it running are different readings of different things, and nothing in the numbers says which is which.

values.why: A modulation the tracker cannot recover from a take it was put into by hand is not evidence that the unit applied none, and nothing in the output separates the two. So every run puts a known modulation into one of its own takes and reports which depths came back. It bounds the run in both directions and neither alone: a null is worth reading only over the depths the control recovered, and a rate found at a depth shallower than the shallowest of those is a fit the tracker was never shown able to make on this material.

eraPriors.claim: A combination effect of this period is built from the same blocks the single effects are, because the blocks are code and memory that already exist and a second copy of a delay line costs both.
eraPriors.why: Carried, not closing. The same prior would have been offered for the bass multi-effect's amp table, and that one reaches a table of its own -- so this is a reason to ask rather than an answer.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: Either combination's comb had sat at a spacing of its own. It is wrong somewhere on this unit already: the bass multi-effect's amp entries sit a median 7.7 dB from the same entries read anywhere else, which is wider than that table's own entries are from each other. So the prior is a reason to ask and the comb is what answers.

alternatives.reading: Each combination carries a delay line of its own, tuned to the same printed range.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Two separately built delays would have to agree with the single type's and with each other at both settings, and the reading resolves them finely enough for that to be a claim: the fit returns 0.618 ms against 1.318 for a delay byte moving from 6 to 13, which is a ratio of 2.133 where the byte's own is 2.167. All eight readings across the two types land on the single type's two figures and on no other.

alternatives.reading: The teeth are a filter of the combination's own rather than a loop, and they happen to sit where the single type's do.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: A comb and a peak are told apart by what happens below the printed nought of the feedback byte. Every profile was scored both as an in-phase comb and as an inverting one, and each of the eight scores at least 1.55 times better on the sign its setting implies -- the settings under the centre on the inverting reading and those over it on the in-phase one. A filter sitting somewhere scores the same both ways.

alternatives.reading: The chorus in front of or beside the flanger is still in the path, and what was read is the two stages together.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Each run wrote the chorus out of the path in the way its own arrangement allows -- the series type's chorus balance to its dry end, the parallel type's chorus level to nothing -- and parked its rate and depth as well. A modulated stage left in the path smears a comb into a shelf, which is what the first published reading of a modulated type came back as; these come back as combs of a single spacing.

alternatives.reading: The two combinations share one delay line with each other but not with the single type.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: They return the single type's figures, not a third pair. There is nothing left for this reading to be about.

alternatives.reading: The half named inside `11 02` agrees on where the comb sits and differs somewhere -- in the modulator, in the balance, or in the output stage. On `02 0B` this is answered for the modulator and the alternative no longer reaches it.

separatedBy.observable: The pitch excursion each type's depth byte buys, read the way the single types' were, and the balance byte's two ends.

predicts.one stage throughout: the combination's depth byte buys the single flanger's excursion at every setting
predicts.the same delay under a different modulat: the excursions differ by more than either repeats to

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: The single types' depth runs repeat to 2.74 per cent and the flanger and the chorus differ there by a ratio from 1.316 to 1.501, so the reading separates two modulators by two orders of magnitude more than it repeats to. The rate the two sides are read at has to be established from the height of the frequency series at a named frequency rather than from the period a picker returns: the two differ by an octave on this type.
separatedBy.why_not_separable: Not by the reading that answered it on the other combination, and the obstruction is in the type rather than in the rig. That reading takes the instantaneous frequency of a partial and reports how far it swings. On the combination where the chorus runs into the flanger the track is what a modulated delay makes of a note, and its excursion agrees with the single type's across the byte. On the one where the chorus sits beside it the same track carries its second harmonic above its fundamental at every setting of the depth byte, which a swept delay alone does not produce: a partial there is a sum of paths, and the frequency of a sum is not the frequency of the modulated one. An excursion read off that track is a smaller number than the delay's own swing and is not the quantity the other side of the comparison carries, so the two cannot be set beside each other however many times either is taken. The archive's other route into a modulator's depth -- counting the comb's notch passages -- does not reach it either, and says so on its own control: asked of a take whose modulator is parked it returns twelve notches where it owes none. What is missing is therefore a reading rather than a booking. The takes this question needs are already recorded, at both of the pre-delays the single types' published excursions were read at, so nothing here waits on the unit.

extra.key: why this is not a round of the single types claim
extra.text: The claim it tests has had three rounds, which is where this project parks one so that a single type cannot absorb the work. And what is claimed here is about two other types: a finding about `02 0B` and `11 02` filed under a file named after `01 23` is a finding nobody looking for those two would find.

extra.key: the reading was corrected before this was scored
extra.text: The bar a tooth has to clear is three times the spread across the run's own repeats of one setting, which is the record's own `floor_db`. It was being taken from the bypass control instead. The two are the same size on the single type -- 3.14 dB against 1.37 -- and they are not on a type whose effect-alone path sits far from its dry one, where the control stands 20.38 dB off while the repeats stand 3.71, and teeth 26 dB deep were being refused by it. A bar that tightens as the effect gets louder is backwards. The correction moved nothing the single type's claim quotes: it returns the same two delays, and two settings it had refused now read and return them as well.

extra.key: why the standing alternative carries no run
extra.text: The model is unchanged. What this recorded is that one of the two readings this archive has into a modulator's depth does not reach one of the types, and that the other fails its own null there -- which moves a queue entry and revises nothing the claim states. A count of rounds that went up for it would spend the last revision this claim is allowed on bookkeeping, and would say the model had been taken further than it has.
